HMPFL WEEK 1 RECAP: LOCKDOWN EDITION

Well, gentlemen, welcome to another sentence — er, season — of His Majesty's Prison Fantasy League. And what a way to kick things off: the entire cell block got slapped with a full lockdown before a single point hit the board. Every scoreboard in the yard reads 0-0. Nobody's move. Nobody's fed. Nobody's fantasy points.

THE CLOSEST GAME (AND ALSO THE BIGGEST BLOWOUT)

In a stunning twist of prison logic, every single matchup this week ended in an exact, dead-even tie — which technically makes it the closest game of the week AND the biggest blowout, depending on which guard you ask. The ConVicks and Ruggs, Drugs and TDs stared each other down 0-0. OJ's Denver Bronco and Rice, Rice Baby ✨ refused to blink, also 0-0. The Adrian BeatHisSons and System of a Brown settled their beef the same way prison arbitration always does: nothing happened. Smack My Diggs Up and Hernandez Hitmen, The Massage Boys and Glove Don't Fit Blitz, and DUIiiiiiiii Dont Know Jim vs. Steve Ruggs all followed suit. Total chaos. Total silence.

STANDOUT PERFORMANCES

Somehow, The ConVicks' entire death row lineup — Jonathon Brooks, Marvin Harrison, Cam Little, George Holani, Woody Marks, Emeka Egbuka, Luther Burden, Tyler Shough, Christian McCaffrey, and even Patrick Mahomes himself — combined for a grand total of zero points. Ten players, zero production. That's not a bye week, that's solitary confinement. Whether this is a scheduling mixup, a system-wide "count time" freeze, or the warden simply forgot to unlock the field, The ConVicks are technically undefeated AND unscored-upon, which in prison terms basically makes them the toughest gang in the yard.

STORYLINES TO WATCH

Is this the calm before the riot? A full week of 0-0 ties smells less like bad luck and more like every inmate in HMPFL is sizing up the competition before the real violence starts in Week 2. Somewhere, a warden (commissioner) is furiously checking the lineup lock times, mumbling about "processing delays" and "the system is down again."

One thing's for certain: nobody made parole this week. Every single manager remains locked at .500, staring at the same blank scoreboard, waiting for the actual games to start counting. Week 2 can't come soon enough — the yard is restless, and somebody's about to get shanked in the standings.
